correctness.rationale: For each strict active record index r, its first physical success time T_r is the unique corresponding strict lazy record time. At T_r, A_{T_r}=r and |A_t-qt|≤D, so each completed active gap and its physical gap obey |qL−ℓ|≤2D; the same applies to the final censored pair with t=n. Re-normalizing physical lengths by n and active lengths by m contributes at most D/(qn) to the 2D/(qn) discrepancy. Sorting matched nonnegative lengths is nonexpansive in sup norm. When the active horizon changes from m to h, all old completed intervals persist; the first new completed interval extends the old censored interval by at most |m−h|, and further new intervals have length at most |m−h|. Sorting and normalization give ||Q_m−Q_h||∞≤2|m−h|/h. Since |m−h|≤D+1, the claimed pathwise bound follows, including m=1 and zero-length censored intervals. For Bernoulli clock increments, the maximal two-sided Hoeffding–Ville inequality P(D>x)≤2 exp(−2x²/n) integrates to E D≤√(πn/2). On m=0 use the trivial distance bound 1 with probability (1−q)^n; all parameters and expectation constants check. Szabó–Vető Theorem 4 exactly covers censored ages of the active symmetric continuous walk, so coordinatewise PD convergence follows by vanishing coupled discrepancy. The independent exact-rational checker passes 118014 finite checks; those do not prove the all-n claim, whose proof is deterministic plus a standard concentration theorem.
residual_risks: The finite-sample comparison is an upper bound with no matching lower bound or sharpness claim.
The coupling rate is O_q(n^{-1/2}) only for fixed q>0; h=0 is intentionally excluded and q→0 is not uniform.
The cited PD theorem establishes coordinatewise/vague convergence, not a total-variation or Wasserstein rate to PD.

originality.rationale: The novel candidate is the explicit, pathwise, simultaneous all-ranks inequality for the censored renewal composition after independent Bernoulli pauses, with a deterministic effective-horizon finite-sample O_q(n^{-1/2}) Wasserstein comparison. The non-lazy PD(1/2,0) theorem itself is Szabó–Vető (2016), not original. Majumdar–Mounaix–Schehr (2021) directly studies the lazy random-walk record model and explicitly poses record ages as further work; its count/correlation formulas do not entail this pathwise estimate. Régnier–Dolgushev–Bénichou (2024) treats general multitime record-count/epoch renewal transforms, not this coupled ranked-age metric in inspected sections. Published record-related database hits concerned different statistics. Best-of-knowledge originality survives, with the possibility of an unindexed general time-change coupling under a different name.
residual_risks: An older generic deterministic stability estimate for ranked renewal compositions under random monotone clocks might imply these constants without being indexed under record ages; absent a located theorem novelty is qualified, not certified.

The 2024 multi-time renewal formalism is broader for joint record-count/epoch observables; the audit inspected relevant formulas and text searches, not every derivation on every page. An undocumented corollary could warrant further comparison.
Classical strong approximation and renewal thinning literature may contain related quantitative random-clock bounds; no exhaustive review of such literature or unpublished work was possible.

value.rationale: Record ages under nonzero staying probability were explicitly left for future study in the 2021 lazy-walk paper. Simultaneous normalized ranked ages are a natural infinite-dimensional observable of the renewal record process, and a deterministic finite-horizon comparison is useful when transferring non-lazy record-age laws and evaluating finite lazy-record samples. The estimate cleanly separates a quantitative clock perturbation from the already-known non-lazy PD limit, and it holds for arbitrary active paths, not only the random-walk corollary. Although the bounding lemmas are elementary and not claimed optimal, their precise coupled full-ranking conclusion addresses a motivated gap rather than a merely renamed computation.
residual_risks: The all-ranks bound may be nonoptimal and is based on standard concentration; no optimality or difficult deeper limit theorem is claimed.
A previously published general renewal time-change lemma could reduce novelty and value; this remains a concrete best-of-knowledge risk.

limitations: Independent finite tests cover n≤9 and the listed q values; they are corroboration, not a universal proof.
